\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Indexed Boolean Fourier numerator]
\lean{FABL.indexedBooleanFourierNumerator}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p025-b004}
\label{FABL.indexedBooleanFourierNumerator}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IndexedSignCube, FABL.Sign}
Let $\iota$ be a finite set, let $g:\{\pm1\}^{\iota}\to\{\pm1\}$, and let
$S\subseteq\iota$. The indexed Boolean Fourier numerator of $g$ at $S$ is
$\sum_{x\in\{\pm1\}^{\iota}} g(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier coefficient as a normalized integer sum]
\lean{FABL.indexedFourierCoeff_toReal_eq_numerator_div}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p025-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p211-b002
}
\label{FABL.indexedFourierCoeff_toReal_eq_numerator_div}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IndexedSignCube, FABL.Sign, FABL.indexedBooleanFourierNumerator, FABL.indexedFourierCoeff, FABL.indexedMonomial, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\iota$ be a finite index set, let $g$ assign a sign to every sign assignment on
$\iota$, and let $S$ be a finite set of indices. The Fourier coefficient of the
real-valued function obtained from $g$ by interpreting its output as a real sign, at
frequency $S$, is the integer sum of $g(x)$ times the product of the input signs in $S$,
interpreted as a real number, divided by the number of sign assignments on $\iota$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Lower bound for a nonzero Fourier coefficient]
\lean{FABL.one_div_card_le_abs_indexedFourierCoeff_toReal_of_ne_zero}
\label{FABL.one_div_card_le_abs_indexedFourierCoeff_toReal_of_ne_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IndexedSignCube, FABL.Sign, FABL.indexedBooleanFourierNumerator, FABL.indexedFourierCoeff, FABL.indexedFourierCoeff_toReal_eq_numerator_div, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be a finite index set, let $g:\{\pm1\}^I\to\{\pm1\}$, and let $S\subseteq I$.
If the Fourier coefficient $\widehat g(S)=\mathbb E_x[g(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$ is nonzero,
then $1/|\{\pm1\}^I|\le |\widehat g(S)|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier coefficients of juntas]
\lean{FABL.fourierCoeff_eq_zero_or_inv_two_pow_le_abs_of_isKJunta}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p156-b006}
\label{FABL.fourierCoeff_eq_zero_or_inv_two_pow_le_abs_of_isKJunta}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.IsKJunta, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.inv_two_pow_card_le_abs_fourierCoeff_of_dependsOn}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f$ be a sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube that depends on at
most $k$ coordinates, and let $S$ be any set of coordinates. Its Fourier coefficient at
$S$ is either zero or has absolute value at least $2^{-k}$.
\end{theorem}
